{{nihongo|'''Izumi Shrine'''|泉神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Hitachi, Ibaraki|Q633922|qid=Q633922}}, {{ill|Ibaraki Prefecture|Q83273|qid=Q83273}}. It is identified with “Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto Shrine” in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}},' and the spring in its precincts is described in the '{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}}' as “Ōi of Mitsuki no Sato.” Izumigamori, the shrine grove of evergreen chinquapin and pines, is designated a Historic Site of Ibaraki Prefecture. {{nihongo|'''Izumi Shrine'''|泉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hitachi Province]].

== Enshrined deity ==
The enshrined deity is the following one<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />.
* Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto (あまのはやたまひめのみこと<ref name="茨城県大百科事典45-46" />)
According to 'Hitachi Nijūhassha-kō,' the Izumi River and sacred jewel are treated as the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}<ref name="茨城県神社誌188-191" />.

Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto is a deity not appearing in the {{ill|Kiki (Shinto)|Q842308|qid=Q842308}}<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />. According to 'Ibaraki Prefecture Shrine Gazetteer,' “Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto is a daughter of Amanotanabatahime-no-Mikoto, consort of {{ill|Futodama|Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|qid=Q11059539|lt=Ame-no-Futodama-no-Mikoto}}, and is also called {{ill|Ame no Hiratome|Q85879124|qid=Q85879124}}”<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />. “Hayatama” in the deity name is an honorific for clear spring water, and the principal deity is thought to be a deification of the spring called Ōi<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. In the 'Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku,' there is mention of “Amanohayatama-no-Kami” without the character for “hime,” but works such as 'Shikinaisha Chōsa Hōkoku' treat it as the same deity as Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto<ref name="式内社調査報告490-496" />.

== History ==
The founding date is unknown<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" /><ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. There is a theory that it was founded in year 49 of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} by Funase no Sukune, the {{ill|Kuji Kokuzō|Q11369664|qid=Q11369664}},<ref name="茨城県神社誌188-191" /> but Funase no Sukune belonged to the time of {{ill|Emperor Seimu|Q316672|qid=Q316672}}, and this has been pointed out as a later fabrication<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />. Izumigamori in the precincts is identified with “Ōi of Mitsuki no Sato” in the Kuji District section of the '{{ill|Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki|Q11481687|qid=Q11481687}},' and Izumi Shrine is identified with “Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto Shrine” listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />. Note that the 'Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki' contains no direct description of Izumi Shrine<ref name="式内社調査報告490-496" />.

According to the '{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Sandai Džicuroku|de|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fa|نیهون ساندای جیتسوروکو|ff|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon sandai jitsuroku|it|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|ko|일본삼대실록|pt|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ru|Нихон сандай дзицуроку|simple|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|zh|日本三代實錄|zh_classical|日本三代實錄|qid=Q1052981}},' Amanohayatama-no-Kami was promoted from Senior Sixth Rank Upper to Junior Fifth Rank Lower on May 27, {{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}} (Jōgan 8), and from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper on December 29, {{ill|874|Q23843|qid=Q23843}} (Jōgan 16)<ref name="角川日本地名大辞典111-112" />. In the '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}},' it is listed in Kuji District, Hitachi Province, as “Amanohayatamahime-no-Mikoto Shrine,” ranked as a minor shrine<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />. After the Meiji Restoration, in April Meiji 6 (1873), it was ranked as a Gōsha under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=modern shrine rank system}}<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />.

According to an extant {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}}, in {{ill|1530|ab|1530|af|1530|als|1530|am|1530 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1530|ar|1530|ary|1530|arz|1530|ast|1530|avk|1530|az|1530|azb|۱۵۳۰ (میلادی)|ban|1530|bar|1530|bcl|1530|be|1530|be_x_old|1530|bg|1530|bn|১৫৩০|bpy|মারি ১৫৩০|br|1530|bs|1530.|ca|1530|cdo|1530 nièng|ceb|1530|ckb|١٥٣٠|crh|1530|cs|1530|cv|1530|cy|1530|da|1530|de|1530|diq|1530|el|1530|eml|1530|eo|1530|es|1530|et|1530|eu|1530|fa|۱۵۳۰ (میلادی)|fi|1530|fo|1530|fr|1530|frr|1530|fur|1530|fy|1530|ga|1530|gan|1530年|gcr|1530|gd|1530|gl|1530|gv|1530|he|1530|hi|१५३०|hif|1530|hr|1530.|ht|1530 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1530|hy|1530|ia|1530|id|1530|ilo|1530|io|1530|is|1530|it|1530|ja|1530年|jv|1530|ka|1530|kaa|1530|kk|1530 жыл|ko|1530년|krc|1530 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1530|la|1530|lb|1530|lfn|1530|lij|1530|lld|1530|lmo|1530|lt|1530 m.|lv|1530. gads|mai|१५३०|map_bms|1530|mdf|1530|mg|1530|mhr|1530|mi|1530|min|1530|mk|1530|mr|इ.स. १५३०|mrj|1530 и|ms|1530|my|၁၅၃၀|nah|1530|nap|1530|nds|1530|new|सन् १५३०|nl|1530|nn|1530|no|1530|nrm|1530|nso|1530|olo|1530|or|୧୫୩୦|os|1530-æм аз|pa|1530|pl|1530|pnb|1530|pt|1530|qu|1530|ro|1530|ru|1530 год|rue|1530|sa|१५३०|sah|1530|sc|1530|scn|1530|sd|1530ع|se|1530|sh|1530.|shn|1530|simple|1530|sk|1530|sl|1530|smn|1530|sq|1530|sr|1530|su|1530|sv|1530|sw|1530|ta|1530|tg|Соли 1530|th|พ.ศ. 2073|tk|1530|tl|1530|tly|1530|tr|1530|tt|1530 ел|uk|1530|ur|1530ء|uz|1530|vec|1530|vi|1530|vls|1530|wa|1530|war|1530|wuu|1530年|xmf|1530|yi|1530|zea|1530|zh|1530年|zh_min_nan|1530 nî|zh_yue|1530年|qid=Q6429}} (Kyōroku 3), {{ill|Satake Yoshiatsu|ja|佐竹義篤 (十六代当主)|qid=Q11383465|lt=Satake Yoshiatsu}} repaired the shrine buildings and changed the shrine title to Izumi Daimyōjin<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. In Eiroku 3, {{ill|Satake Yoshiaki|it|Satake Yoshiaki|ja|佐竹義昭|pt|Satake Yoshiaki|zh|佐竹義昭|qid=Q11383447}} reroofed the buildings, and in the Edo period, under Mito Domain protection, construction was carried out on June 26, Kan'en 3<ref name="角川日本地名大辞典111-112" />. Later, the shrine buildings burned down in the Kyōwa era (1801–1804) and were rebuilt in the Bunka era (1804–1818)<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. In 1960 (Shōwa 35), they burned down again, and a temporary shrine building was constructed in 1961 (Shōwa 36)<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. According to 'Hitachi Taga-gun-shi,' before the loss, the main sanctuary was 9 shaku wide and 8 shaku deep, and the worship hall was 4 ken 3 shaku in front and 2 ken 3 shaku in depth<ref name="式内社調査報告490-496" />.

== Precincts ==
[[File:Izumi Jinja Hitachi Honden.jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Main sanctuary}}]]
The precinct area is 1,185 tsubo (3,917 m²), and the outside-owned land is 6,655 tsubo (22,000 m²)<ref name="茨城県神社誌188-191" />. The shrine buildings constructed in 1961 (Shōwa 36) are: a reinforced-concrete nagare-zukuri main sanctuary, 1 ken 2 shaku wide and 2 ken deep; and a worship hall with corrugated-metal-roof irimoya-zukuri, 3 ken 3 shaku wide and 3 ken deep<ref name="式内社調査報告490-496" />.

The entire Izumi Shrine precinct is called Izumigamori and is designated a historic site of Ibaraki Prefecture<ref name="角川日本地名大辞典111-112" />. It consists of evergreen trees such as chinquapin and pine<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. The “Ōi of Mitsuki no Sato” in the Kuji District section of the 'Hitachi no Kuni Fudoki' is identified with Izumigamori<ref name="茨城県大百科事典45-46" />. In the northeast part of Izumigamori is a spring with a circumference of about 40 meters and maximum depth of about 2 meters<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />. This spring deepens sharply toward the center like a mortar and has more than 20 spring vents of various sizes<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />.

== Precinct shrines ==
Precinct shrines are as follows<ref>{{Cite web|ja|date= |url=http://izumi-jinja.sakura.ne.jp/Yuisyo-Page.html |title=History of Izumi Shrine |publisher=Izumi Shrine |accessdate=2015-7-13}}</ref>.
* Itsukushima Shrine - Ichikishimahime-no-Mikoto
* Mitsumine Shrine - Izanagi-no-Kami, Izanami-no-Kami
* Sagimori Shrine - Amatamahashiraya-hime-no-Mikoto
* Fuji Shrine - Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto
* Hōnen Shrine - Tsukuyomi-no-Mikoto, Ōanamuchi-no-Mikoto
* Inari Shrine - Uka-no-Mitama-no-Ōkami

== Festivals ==
[[File:Mikoshiden of Izumi-jinja (Hitachi).jpg|thumb|250px|right|{{center|Mikoshi hall}}]]
* New Year Festival - January 1<ref name="茨城県神社誌188-191" />
* Tsuina Festival - February 3<ref name="茨城県神社誌188-191" />
* Spring Festival (Kinen-sai) - February 11<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />
* Tōya Festival - old calendar Feb. 12–14<ref name="茨城県の地名100-101" />
* Annual Festival - May 3<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />
* Autumn Festival (Niiname-sai) - November 23<ref name="茨城の神社覚書I137-139" />

== Cultural properties ==
== Prefecture-designated Intangible Folk Cultural Property ==
* Hitachi no Sasara - designated August 23, 1963 (Shōwa 38)<ref name="茨城の神社覚書II228-230" />.
== Prefecture-designated Historic Site ==
* {{ill|Izumigamori|ja|泉が森|qid=Q11554674}} - designated December 1, 1969 (Shōwa 44)<ref name="茨城の神社覚書II228-230" />.
